trust_decision.summary: Whether untrusted request content (query values, path, non-excluded headers, body, top-level JSON string fields) matches the suspicious-pattern list, which decides block/auto-ban in penetration detection; the 3.0.1 length bounds ({0,1000}, {1,200}...) let payloads longer than the bound go undetected.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'regex bypass' from length limits; the bounded-quantifier pattern list is the obvious place, and the first pattern is the bounded <script> rule.

fix_sites.entry_point: SecurityMiddleware.dispatch (any HTTP route) -> detect_penetration_attempt; also public SusPatternsManager.get_all_compiled_patterns
public API guard.utils.detect_penetration_attempt (JSON-dict branch), called by middleware
public API detect_penetration_attempt signature gains regex_timeout
SecurityMiddleware.dispatch, every HTTP request when penetration detection is enabled
SecurityConfig construction (new regex_timeout field, ge=0.1 le=30.0)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Every changed site is on the single middleware -> detect_penetration_attempt -> pattern-list path; middleware.py:340 is a direct caller, not a separate implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue that bounded quantifiers were the deliberate fix for the earlier ReDoS advisory (CHANGELOG.md:6-13), so removing them is out of scope and regresses ReDoS; they may also tighten only the <script> pattern they reproduced and leave the other ~35 bounded patterns.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: ReDoS resistance from the prior fix: removing the length bounds without a time/size guard brings catastrophic backtracking back (e.g. the nested-group URL pattern); and an over-broad fix (rejecting all long inputs, or scanning the deliberately excluded headers) produces false positives on benign large bodies and normal headers.

O6_input_shapes: top-level string fields of a JSON object body/value (guard/utils.py:380-383)
user-added custom patterns, which also go through the same search sites (guard/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py:284-294)

O7_producer.where: Patterns are compiled in SusPatternsManager.__new__ (guard/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py:128-133), which the check reads through get_all_compiled_patterns (guard/utils.py:373); no separate schema/serializer stage.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A length-bounded pattern idiom (or truncation of the value before search) inside the add_pattern / custom-pattern compilation path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer hardening against ReDoS could wrap or truncate user-supplied custom patterns here, recreating the same length bypass in a second code path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Custom patterns reloaded from Redis are split on ',' so any pattern with a {m,n} quantifier is corrupted on save/reload
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Real code at the pinned commit (join on save at guard/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py:170); a planted test could require bounded custom patterns to survive reload, a save/reload how-type sibling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Value truncation / max-length cap applied before pattern search in check_value (e.g. body[:N])
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A plausible 'performance' guard a maintainer adds next to the ReDoS bounds; it is the same length-bypass mechanism in the caller rather than in the patterns.

O9_family: CWE-185 incorrect regex / detection bypass via length-bounded quantifiers (paired with the CWE-1333 ReDoS trade-off)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Raise the {0,1000}/{1,200} bounds on the <script> pattern only (or on the reproduced pattern) instead of removing bounds across the list and adding a time guard.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit d9d50e8 (the earlier GHSA-j47q-rc62-w448 bounded-quantifier fix) is already an ancestor of the pinned commit (CHANGELOG.md:6-13 shows v3.0.1); only 0829292 is the effective fix here.

check_value scans only top-level str values of JSON objects; JSON arrays, nested objects and JSON-string bodies return no-match without scanning (guard/utils.py:380-388), a shape bypass not tied to length.
Starlette query_params.items() yields one value per repeated key, so other values of a repeated query key are not scanned (guard/utils.py:396).
The published fix fails open on timeout (returns False) and the worker thread cannot be cancelled, so long inputs can still evade detection (fix.diff:464-478).

User-agent and behaviour-rule regexes use re.search with no timeout (guard/utils.py:212, guard/middleware.py:519, guard/handlers/behavior_handler.py:212); these are config-supplied patterns in a separate feature.
